clue.text: Spice Girls upset with an Australian town

indicators.note: something upset is knocked over and thrown into disorder, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the pop group's name taken letter for letter
taken as written

explanation.surface: A girl band is in a sour mood on tour in a small Australian outback town.
explanation.definitionFit: Alice Springs is a well-known settlement in the Northern Territory, in the middle of the outback.

clue.text: Copper admitted to terrible scare for plaintiff

indicators.note: terrible suggests a mess, so the following word's letters are thrown into a new order
something admitted to a place is let inside it, so one piece goes within the other

blocks.note: taken as written before rearranging
Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

explanation.surface: A police officer lets slip a frightening story that helps the person bringing a case.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Copper' reads as a policeman, but it is the metal, whose symbol sits inside the rearranged scare.
explanation.definitionFit: A plaintiff brings a charge against someone in court, which makes them an accuser.

clue.text: Disregards sovereign or established borders

indicators.note: the letters wanted lie along the borders where these words meet, straddling their edges

blocks.note: found running across the end of the first word, the whole of the second and the start of the third

explanation.surface: A monarch, or perhaps a long-settled state, defines its frontiers.
explanation.definitionFit: To ignore something is to pay no attention to it, the same as disregarding it.

clue.text: High-spirited English farm animal on cover of impressive books

indicators.note: the cover of something is its outside, so only the first and last letters of the word are used

blocks.note: standard abbreviation for English
a male bovine kept on a farm
the outside letters of this word
NT is the New Testament, a set of books of the Bible

explanation.surface: A cheerful English beast stands on the jacket of some splendid volumes.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'on' means the first part sits above the rest. NT is the usual crossword abbreviation for the New Testament.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone ebullient is bubbling over with enthusiasm and cheerful energy.

clue.text: Great deal following leader of Ponzi scheme

indicators.note: the leader of a word is the letter at its front, so only that first letter is taken
one piece following another means it is written after it in the answer

blocks.note: the opening letter of this name
a lot is a great deal

explanation.surface: A huge sum flows in behind the man fronting a fraudulent investment scam.
explanation.walkthrough: A Ponzi scheme pays early investors with money from later ones, so the surface is all about fraud.
explanation.definitionFit: A plot is a secret plan or scheme, often an underhand one.

clue.text: Fish in hostelry — starter of tuna using a lot of sauce?

indicators.note: one thing in another sits inside it, so the fish goes within the hostelry
a starter comes first, so only the opening letter of the word is taken

blocks.note: an inn is a hostelry
the sole is a flat fish
the first letter of this word

explanation.surface: A pub menu offers fish, then tuna drowned in a heavy sauce.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sauce' is the British sense of cheek or impudence, so heavy use of it is rudeness, not a cookery note; the question mark flags the pun.
explanation.definitionFit: Insolent means rude and disrespectful, and sauce is informal British for cheeky impertinence.

clue.text: Screen icon's boast about Oscar

indicators.note: about can mean turned round, so the word is read backwards

blocks.note: to brag is to boast
Oscar is O in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A film star crows about winning an Academy Award.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Oscar' invites thoughts of the film award, but it is just the radio code word for O.
explanation.definitionFit: Greta Garbo was a Swedish-born Hollywood star, a leading icon of the silver screen.

clue.text: Compel ignoble criminal to drop name

indicators.note: dropping something leaves it behind, so that letter is taken out
something criminal is crooked, so the letters are bent into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
N is the abbreviation for name

explanation.surface: Force a disreputable crook to stop using his alias.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove the N from the base word, then rearrange the six letters left.
explanation.definitionFit: To oblige someone can mean to force or require them to do something.

clue.text: Journey from Finland's capital requiring little effort

indicators.note: a capital letter is the one at the head of a word, so only the initial is taken

blocks.note: the opening letter of this country's name
light work needs little effort

explanation.surface: A trip out of Helsinki that turns out to be easy going.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Finland's capital' looks like Helsinki, but it means the capital letter of Finland.
explanation.definitionFit: A flight is a trip made by aeroplane, a kind of journey.

clue.text: Illusionists deceive people in court

blocks.note: to con is to deceive
members of a jury sitting in a courtroom

explanation.surface: Stage magicians trick the twelve good citizens hearing a trial.
explanation.definitionFit: Conjurors perform magic tricks that create illusions for an audience.

clue.text: Some film about Brando, initially — or James Dean?

indicators.note: initially points to the beginning, so just the first letter of the name is taken
about means surrounding, so one piece wraps around the other

blocks.note: a reel is a length of film
the opening letter of the actor's surname

explanation.surface: A movie about Marlon Brando, or maybe about James Dean instead.
explanation.walkthrough: James Dean starred in Rebel Without a Cause, so he is offered as an example, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: James Dean's famous screen role made him the archetype of the restless young rebel.

clue.text: Certainly backing American bank

indicators.note: backing means going backwards, so the word is read from end to start

blocks.note: US is short for American
to bank on is to rely on

explanation.surface: Surely you would support a US financial institution?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bank' looks like a noun for a lender; here it is the verb as in bank on someone.
explanation.definitionFit: Surely is an adverb of confidence, used just like certainly or undoubtedly.

clue.text: Granting adult 50 pounds, having debts

blocks.note: A is the film-rating abbreviation for adult
L is the Roman numeral for fifty
L is the abbreviation for pounds sterling, from Latin libra
someone owing money has debts

explanation.surface: Handing a grown-up fifty quid while they are in the red.
explanation.definitionFit: Allowing a request means permitting it, which is the same as granting it.

clue.text: More impetuous, and a bit of a pig?

blocks.note: first meaning: comparative of an adjective for acting without thought
second meaning: a thin slice of bacon

explanation.surface: Someone rather reckless who is also somewhat greedy and piggish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A bit of a pig' sounds like a mild insult, but it is literal: a slice from a pig.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both the comparative of rash, meaning hastier, and a noun for a slice of bacon.

clue.text: Most cross strange ground around India

indicators.note: something ground is crushed and broken up, so the letters are mixed into a new order
around means surrounding, so the rearranged letters enclose the extra one

blocks.note: taken as written before rearranging
India is I in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: The angriest people are on odd land surrounding an Asian country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'strange ground' reads as odd terrain; in fact 'strange' is the fodder and 'ground' the mixing signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Being cross means being annoyed, so the most cross person is the angriest one.

clue.text: Concerned with undergraduate kind of course

blocks.note: re means regarding or concerning
a fresher is a first-year university student

explanation.surface: A first-year student is interested in a particular type of study programme.
explanation.walkthrough: Fresher is British slang for a new university student.
explanation.definitionFit: A refresher course updates knowledge already gained, a familiar type of training course.

clue.text: Aversion is stated in an alternative form

indicators.note: an alternative form means the same material shaped differently, so the letters are reordered

blocks.note: taken as written before rearranging

explanation.surface: A dislike is expressed in a different way.
explanation.definitionFit: Distaste is a feeling of dislike or repugnance, which is what an aversion is.

clue.text: Keep most important article in can

indicators.note: one thing in another sits inside it, so the article goes within the can

blocks.note: the main thing is the most important
a tin is a can
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: Store your most valuable item inside a tin.
explanation.definitionFit: To maintain something is to keep it going or keep it in good order.

clue.text: Coat put on friend of Harry or Emmanuel?

blocks.note: a mac is a raincoat, short for mackintosh
Ron Weasley is Harry Potter's best friend

explanation.surface: A coat is worn by a pal of Prince Harry, or perhaps by someone named Emmanuel.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'put on' means the first part sits on top of the second. The question mark marks Emmanuel as one example of the surname.
explanation.definitionFit: Emmanuel Macron is President of France, so his surname is defined by his first name.

clue.text: Spoil broadcast fronted by mischief-maker

indicators.note: being fronted by something means it stands at the front, so that piece is written first

blocks.note: an imp is a mischievous little sprite
to air a programme is to broadcast it

explanation.surface: A prankster ruins a radio or television programme.
explanation.definitionFit: To impair something is to damage or weaken it, so to spoil it.

clue.text: Make up for regularly missing golf, if asked to

indicators.note: missing at regular intervals means skipping every other letter, keeping the rest

blocks.note: the second, fourth, sixth and following even letters

explanation.surface: Compensate for skipping your round of golf now and then when asked.
explanation.definitionFit: To offset a loss is to counterbalance it, which is making up for it.

clue.text: Massage received by Rishi at summerhouse

indicators.note: something received by the words is held within them, so the answer is sitting inside

blocks.note: found running across the end of the name, the whole short word and the start of the last

explanation.surface: Rishi Sunak is given a rubdown in his garden pavilion.
explanation.definitionFit: Shiatsu is a Japanese form of therapeutic massage using finger pressure.

clue.text: Soil is hard underneath mountain lake

indicators.note: in a down answer, what lies underneath is written below, so the later pieces come after

blocks.note: a tarn is a small lake in the mountains
taken as written
H is the pencil-grading abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: Firm earth lies beneath a lake high in the hills.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Soil' looks like a noun for earth, but it is the verb meaning to stain.
explanation.definitionFit: To tarnish is to dull or stain, so soil something, often a reputation.

clue.text: Limit a built-up area's dimensions

blocks.note: a cap is a limit, as in a spending cap
taken as written
a city is a large built-up area

explanation.surface: Restrict the size of a town's sprawl.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for has, joining the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Capacity is the size or volume something can hold, a matter of its dimensions.

clue.text: Tom maybe arresting that man, a swindler

indicators.note: arresting someone means seizing and holding them, so one piece is held inside the other

blocks.note: a tom is a male cat
he refers to that man

explanation.surface: Perhaps a policeman called Tom is detaining that fellow, a con artist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tom' looks like a person's name, but it is a tomcat; 'maybe' signals an example.
explanation.definitionFit: A cheat is someone who deceives others for gain, which is what a swindler does.

clue.text: Older Spanish gent accommodating the crossword setter

indicators.note: accommodating someone means giving them room inside, so one piece holds the other

blocks.note: señor is Spanish for a gentleman
the setter refers to themselves as I

explanation.surface: An elderly Spanish gentleman puts up the person who wrote this puzzle.
explanation.definitionFit: Senior is a comparative meaning greater in age, the same as older.

clue.text: Spiteful remark from Ken's partner that is dismissed

indicators.note: something dismissed is sent away, so those letters are taken out

blocks.note: Ken is the boyfriend doll of Barbie
i.e. is the abbreviation for that is

explanation.surface: A catty comment from a man's girlfriend gets her thrown out.
explanation.definitionFit: A barb is a cutting, hurtful comment, like the sharp point on a hook.

clue.text: Perhaps sheepish individual catching classical sextet

indicators.note: catching something means holding it within, so one piece goes inside the other

blocks.note: one is a single individual
VI is six in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A shy person catches a group of six musicians playing classical music.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sheepish' usually means embarrassed; 'Perhaps' tells you to read it literally as of sheep. 'Classical' points to Roman numerals.
explanation.definitionFit: Ovine means relating to sheep, a literal sense of sheepish.

clue.text: Time to board a ship — get revised fare from Italy

indicators.note: boarding a vessel means getting inside it, so the extra letter joins the other letters
something revised is reworked, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: T is the abbreviation for time
taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: It is time to embark on a cruise liner and try the Italian menu.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fare' means food here, not a ticket price.
explanation.definitionFit: Spaghetti is the classic Italian pasta, so it is food from Italy.

clue.text: Wildlife presenter in Croydon, say, following when the evening news is on

indicators.note: one piece following another means it is written after it in the answer

blocks.clueFragment: when the evening news is on
blocks.note: News at Ten is ITV's long-running evening news bulletin
Croydon is one of the London boroughs

explanation.surface: A nature broadcaster in a south London suburb catches the late evening bulletin.
explanation.walkthrough: Croydon is a London borough, a local government district; News at Ten is a British television news programme.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir David Attenborough is the famous British broadcaster of natural history documentaries.
